analysis.title: Global Macro / Goal Kickstart / Apple / Allianz / DSV / Gjensidige / M&A Basket / Unibail / Building Mats / Solaria / Argenx
key_insights: Global growth has been unremarkable in 2026, with fiscal easing and the AI boom offsetting drags from energy and tariffs. GS baseline is a similar pace in 2027, with downside risks building from higher energy prices, higher bond yields and possibly slower AI investment growth next year.
GS expects fewer rate hikes than priced for most major DM central banks, as AI labor market effects become more visible and inflation is likely to decline.
GOAL Kickstart: the Risk Appetite Indicator is negative as Tech dominates cross-asset moves. GS remains modestly pro-risk: OW Equities (3m/12m), UW Credit (3m/12m), OW Cash (3m), OW Bonds (12m).
AI concerns, Middle East tensions and mid-term elections could sustain near-term volatility. GS expects earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations to help equities into year-end.

AAPL F4Q26 preview: GS expects in-line results. iPhone revenue +15% y/y on price increases on iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max and older models plus the Duo launch, offsetting modest volume declines. Services revenue +10% y/y. Gross margin 47.8%, including a 1pp benefit from tariff refunds and component cost inflation headwinds.

Allianz reports 3Q'26 on November 12. GS operating profit estimate is c.1% below company-collected consensus (published 26/10/26), driven by P&C (-2%) and Asset Management (-2%). The lower P&C estimate reflects a c.15bps less favourable headline COR and c.2% lower Insurance Revenue.

DSV: Buy reiterated, 12m DCF-based PT unchanged at DKK 2,300. 2026-30 estimate changes are limited (EPS slightly down, FCF slightly up, +/-2% on average). Q3'26 EBIT was DKK 6.3bn versus ~DKK 4bn per quarter when the DBS deal was announced in 2024. GS expects DKK 7-8bn quarterly EBIT during 2027, with Road running c. DKK 1bn per quarter behind schedule.

Gjensidige downgraded to Neutral as pricing normalises and claims inflation moderates, leaving limited room to beat high expectations. Prior pricing actions still support profitability, but margin expansion should be more measured. FY27e-30e EPS cut by c.2.4% on average.

GS rebalanced its European M&A basket (GSTRACQN). Additions: Abivax, Haleon, Moncler, Burberry, Prada, Swatch Group, Rightmove, Scout24 and Zegona. c.65% of the basket is Industrials, Consumer Discretionary and Healthcare, with c.35% UK-domiciled.

Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield: Buy maintained after 9M26 results. 2026E-2030E EPS cut 0-2% on higher refinancing costs. Management reiterated 2028 guidance but closer to the lower end. 12m PT lowered 2% to EUR 121.0 (from EUR 124.0), implying 34% upside.

Also covered by title only, with no detail in the text: European building materials (US residential roofing supply/demand challenges), Solaria (a 'fundamental dislocation') and Argenx (management roadshow on Vyvgart growth).
